subject: Availability exception runbook & SLA proposal for Zenova
messages:
From: Asha Patel <asha@zenova.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Zenova Procurement <procurement@zenova.ai>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@zenova.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — availability & p95 SLA for Zenova production rollout

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving this integration toward pilot with our search & recommendations service and need to lock down the operational commitments to proceed. Specifically:

- Target uptime: 99.995% monthly (we know this is higher than your standard plan; asking as an exception for a pilot-to-production runway)
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms for typical text-gen endpoints at our 50 req/s steady-state load
- Incident window & credits: we need a clear credit schedule and a runbook that shows how Redwood will ramp or failover if the SLO is at risk

Can you put together a short runbook and a draft SLA we can share with procurement? Also please call out any hardware or Dedicated capacity requirements and expected incremental spend.

Asha
Head of Integrations, Zenova AI
asha@zenova.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Initial ask — availability & p95 SLA for Zenova production rollout

Team — forwarding Zenova's ask (below). High-level notes: 99.995% and p95 120ms at 50 rps is aggressive but not necessarily impossible if we combine Dedicated capacity + burst reservation + prefix caching. Need input on:

1) Serving constraints: how much Dedicated GPU pool sizing to guarantee p95 at 120ms with model X-2 (they plan to use our curated x2-13b variant)
2) Fallbacks: recommended product-level fallbacks (model downgrade, soft degradation, degraded feature set) and how we instrument automatic failover
3) Credits and escalation: Laura, can you propose a credit table and conditions for exception?
4) Runbook: Monica/Marcus — can you draft an operational playbook that outlines canary, autoscale thresholds, and manual escalation steps (SRE pager flow)?

I'm aiming to send a consolidated response to Asha tomorrow EOD with a draft SLA attached.

Thanks — Karthik
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial ask — availability & p95 SLA for Zenova production rollout

Karthik / team — technically here's where we land after a quick sizing pass: 

- Model & HW: For x2-13b at 50 rps with p95 120ms we should provision a Dedicated pool of 4x A100-class instances with reserved burst of 2x for peak bursts. That assumes batching tuned to 8-12 tokens average and prefix cache enabled.
- Graceful degradation: Recommend a two-tier fallback: 1) auto-downgrade to x2-7b (quantized) if queuing latency > 80ms for 30s; 2) route to hosted fallback with reduced context (soft-fail) if Dedicated pool is unhealthy for > 3m. This lets us preserve availability while controlling cost.
- Canary & rollout: Canary at 10% traffic for 24h with synthetic load; then 50% for 6h; full roll at 72h post green. KV cache warm-up must be included in canary plan.
- Observability: Add token-level latency histograms, per-route p95 alert, and a dedicated Zenova dashboard.

Attached a short operational playbook (operational-playbook-zenova.xlsx) with runbook steps, escalation flow, and recommended alert thresholds. Two open questions: does legal want a hard credit schedule or a discretionary one we can negotiate? Also need a SRE on-call name to add to the runbook.

— Marcus
Senior Architect, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
(attachment: operational-playbook-zenova.xlsx)
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial ask — availability & p95 SLA for Zenova production rollout

Thanks — reviewed Marcus' playbook. For procurement negotiation:

- Credits: propose a tiered credit schedule tied to uptime bands (example): 99.995+ = 0% credits; 99.99-99.995 = 5% monthly credit; 99.9-99.99 = 15% credit; <99.9 = 40% credit. These are monetary credits off monthly usage.
- Exceptions: we can offer an "exception" contract offering if Zenova commits to a 12-month Dedicated reservation (or equivalent committed spend) and accepts the fallback matrix (downgrade & hosted fallback).
- Escalation & auditability: require weekly uptime reports for first 90 days and shared SLO dashboard access. Also propose a 30-day termination right if service repeatedly fails to meet the agreed SLO.

I'll draft a short SLA (see attached draft-SLA-zenova-v1.pdf) with the above and leave placeholders for credit amounts and exact Dedicated sizing. We should align on the rollback policy Marcus suggested — legal needs the failover behavior explicit so procurement can accept.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success (Contracts)
Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft-SLA-zenova-v1.pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha@zenova.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Zenova Procurement <procurement@zenova.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — availability & p95 SLA for Zenova production rollout

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a consolidated proposal and an operational runbook for your review. Summary of our recommended approach: 

- Commitment: We can support an exception to the standard SLA if Zenova signs a 12-month Dedicated reservation (or equivalent committed spend).
- Availability & latency: With the Dedicated pool configuration proposed by Marcus (4x reserved + 2x burst) plus prefix caching and the canary rollout described, we are confident we can target effective monthly availability approaches 99.995 and p95 ~120ms under the steady-state load. We will include the exact hardware sizing and a tuning window in the SLA.
- Fallbacks & rollback: If latency or queueing is sustained above thresholds we will first auto-downgrade to the quantized x2-7b variant (preserves responses, reduces cost) and then route a fraction of traffic to our hosted fallback after 3m if the Dedicated pool remains unhealthy. These steps are codified in the attached operational-playbook.
- Credits & governance: Laura recommends a tiered credit table (see draft SLA). We propose weekly SLO reviews for the first 90 days and a joint post-mortem process for incidents that breach the SLA.

Next steps: would you and procurement be open to a 30-minute technical deep-dive this week to confirm Dedicated sizing? If so, send a few time slots and we'll invite Marcus and an SRE to join.

Sharing attachments: draft-SLA-zenova-v1.pdf, operational-playbook-zenova.xlsx

Thanks — Karthik
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
